newsitem.title: USA: Bronx, N.Y. Faberware plant wins judicial reprieve.
newsitem.headline: Bronx, N.Y. Faberware plant wins judicial reprieve.

text.p: The Faberware plant in the Bronx, N.Y., which employs as many as 700 workers, won a partial reprieve from a judge, who ordered it to remain open for another five days with about 120 employees.

The city and state, which took the plant to court to keep it open, also got an agreement in principle to keep it open through December 8 with an unspecified number of workers, while they look for new investors, said a state official. Judge

Douglas McKeon, a state Supreme Court judge, issued his ruling on September 13, and the two companies involved must soon give him a plan to keep the plant open, added John Melia, a spokesman for the Empire State Development Corp.

A pact between Syratech Corp, which owns the plant's capital equipment, and US Industries, which is responsible for the firm's operations, expired in early September and only Syratech had agreed to a 90-day extension.

The plant, which will not be able to use the Faberware name, will be toured on Tuesday by the judge, equipment manufacturers, and potential investors, which include a New York City fund which has $50 million of private money.
